parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Construct an equation for the **second** ionisation energy of argon.

parts.label: (b)
(c)
parts.text:
The energy value required to remove the first electron from an atom of argon is circled on the graph.

Sketch the shape of the orbital that contains this electron.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Chlorine exists as a diatomic gas, $\text{Cl}_2\text{(g)}$. A sample of $\text{Cl}_2\text{(g)}$ was made during a chemical reaction. When measured at $404\text{ kPa}$ and $25^{\circ}\text{C}$ the sample occupied a volume of $20.0\text{ cm}^3$.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text:
Calculate the mass, in grams, of $\text{Cl}_2\text{(g)}$ formed.

For this calculation, assume that chlorine behaves as an ideal gas under these conditions.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
Calculate the number of chlorine atoms in this sample of $\text{Cl}_2\text{(g)}$. You may find it helpful to use your answer to **(d)(i)**.

If you are unable to calculate an answer to **(d)(i)**, use $0.36\text{ g}$ of $\text{Cl}_2$. This is **not** the correct answer.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text:
$\text{Cl}_2\text{(g)}$ does **not** behave as an ideal gas under these conditions.

Explain why $\text{Cl}_2\text{(g)}$ behaves even **less** ideally at:

- very high pressures

- very low temperatures.
